newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann lower, mobile sales disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann lower, mobile sales disappoint.

text.p: Shares in German engineering company Mannesmann AG fell on Tuesday after it reported nine month figures, with some analysts saying sales from its mobile telecommunications arm were seen as disappointing.
Shares in Mannesmann fell 6.60 marks ($4.39) to 620.40 in electronic IBIS trade after the figures. In early bourse trading it was 1.50 marks lower at 621 marks.
Meanwhile the DAX index of 30 leading shares was slightly firmer, up 6.03 points at 2,769.87 by 0950 GMT.

"It looks like the net additions to its (D2 mobile telephone) network in the third quarter disappointed because they were lower than in the preceding quarters," Niall O' Connor, analyst at CS First Boston in London said.
He added that this could have been compounded by concern over the impact of a new lower pricing policy for its telecom service on margins.
"But it should not be too worrying in the long-term," he said, noting that price erosion in mobile telephony was an expected and normal development.
Mannesmann earlier said nine-month sales rose six percent to 23.9 billion marks. It cited its telecommunications and automotive operations as the main drivers of the growth.
